Per BUILD_PROGRESS.md, the next thing is exactly what the slice's own closing paragraph names: the guest staging area and /table/{id}'s living-order view (§11.1) — the first consumer of the engine.

The slice I'd designed
New files

Sibling to OrderProjection, held in step by a test asserting its non-removed lines equal OrderProjection's. (written)
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Orders/OrderStaging.cs — the pure basket: stage/unstage/quantity, mark-for-removal, PruneRemovals (so a stale tick can't sink an all-or-nothing batch), Build(IIdentifierFactory) returning operations plus parallel descriptions for the rejection panel. (written)
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Orders/MoneyText.cs — RESTAURANT_CURRENCY_CODE-driven formatting, since ToString("C") would silently ignore the configured code. (written)

Two findings worth flagging now:

F-36 — timestamps ignore RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE. Every surface uses .ToLocalTime(), which is the server process zone; your container sets no TZ, so guests would see UTC. §13 also never settles 12- vs 24-hour. I'd record it and fix every surface in one dedicated slice rather than leaving two conventions on one page.
A closed-then-reopened sitting on the same table makes GetOpenSittingForMemberAsync return the new sitting — the settled-view check has to compare identifiers, not just null-ness.
